Is there a separate refresh we need to run after applying credit notes? Please don't remove the payment from the first example while investigating; that part appears to be reflected correctly.

report.title: Late-money screen isn't picking up our write-downs
report.description: The collections overview says Fernspindle Workshop owes us 900, but their bill page says 650. We gave them a 250 reduction memo for cancelled artwork and linked it to that bill. The 61–90 day column still contains all 900. Cash receipts change the figure on this screen straight away; reductions for cancelled work don't seem to change it at all. Our finance person is having to cross-check each customer before sending reminders.

report.title: Credited sums still showing as overdue
report.description: The overdue totals still include the bits we've already cleared with credit notes, even though the invoices show the reduced balances.

report.title: Release 7.14 broke our receivables figures
report.description: I'm blaming Quillnest 7.14 for this because we first spotted it after the release banner appeared yesterday. Our aged-receivables view is too high whenever an invoice has an applied credit note. Example: £1,000 invoice, £200 paid, £300 credited. The invoice itself correctly says £500 due, while the aging row says £800. Payments seem to come through normally; the credit is the bit missing from the calculation. It's happening on older invoices as well as one we adjusted this morning. Please can you roll back whatever changed in 7.14? We use those age buckets for our Monday collections meeting and can't trust the totals right now.

report.title: Client search keeps forgetting my filter
report.description: The aged-receivables dashboard is working fine for us: applied credit notes reduce the outstanding invoice amount, and none of the age buckets overstate the debt. My actual issue is the client directory. If I select 'Active clients only,' open a client, then go back, that filter resets to 'All clients.' I'd like it to remember my selection.

report.title: Long invoice notes get cut off when printing from the browser
report.description: Pasting this from our studio's Slack: In QuillHarbor, an invoice with more than a page of notes loses the end of those notes when we print directly from the browser. The print preview already shows the cutoff, so it isn't our printer running out of paper. The invoice total is still there, but the last few paragraphs of our payment conditions aren't. If I download the invoice PDF instead, all the notes are included. Shorter notes print fine. We need the browser print option to include the whole text, even when it runs onto another page.

report.title: Paper copy stops halfway through our extra wording
report.description: Could someone look at the hard-copy layout for billing statements? We put quite a bit of handover guidance and payment wording below the charges. It is all visible on the web screen, but using the menu command to send that screen to paper gives us only the first sheet's worth of that section. The rest never appears on a following sheet. It ends mid-sentence, with no indication that anything is missing. Choosing the separate save-as-file option and opening that document gives us every paragraph, so the wording hasn't been deleted. We can use that route for now, but our accounts assistant normally works straight from the open statement and has already sent one incomplete copy to a client.

report.title: Extra terms missing on paper
report.description: The end of our multi-page invoice notes is missing from the browser's paper copy, but it's there in the saved PDF.

report.title: Release 7.14 broke browser printing for detailed invoices
report.description:
I'm pretty convinced this came with QuillHarbor 7.14. That's the release number shown in our workspace, and we only noticed this after the update banner appeared. Please check whatever changed in that release's invoice layout.

We're a four-person design studio and sometimes include a fairly substantial set of licensing conditions in the invoice notes. For this job, the notes cover usage rights, delivery milestones, third-party assets, and what happens if the client requests source files later. On screen, every paragraph is present. Nothing is missing when I reopen the draft or the issued invoice.

The trouble starts when I use the browser's Print command. The preview shows the beginning of the notes, then stops partway through the licensing section. There should be enough text to continue onto another page, but that continuation just isn't there. The paper output matches the preview. I tried a second printer because I initially thought ours was dropping a page; it produced the same incomplete result.

Downloading the invoice as a PDF gives me the complete wording across multiple pages. I can print that file successfully, too. A different invoice with just two sentences in the notes also works through the browser, which is why we missed this during our usual checks.

We've told everyone to use the download route for now. Still, please roll back the 7.14 printing change if you can. We shouldn't have to compare the last sentence on every paper invoice against the screen before posting it.

report.title: Invoice search forgets the query when I return
report.description: Browser printing is fine for us now: long invoice notes aren't clipped, and both the printed copy and downloaded PDF contain everything. That's not what this ticket is about. My complaint is that the invoice search box clears itself whenever I open a result and go back to the list. I have to type the client reference again each time. Please keep the search query when returning from an invoice.

report.title: Undone reimbursement is gone, but the expenses still say Paid
report.description: We recorded a reimbursement for three approved expense claims in Dovetailoop, then undid it because we had selected the wrong payment account. The reimbursement transaction disappeared, which is what we expected, but all three claims are still marked Paid. When we try to create a new reimbursement with the correct account, those claims aren't available to select. Nobody has actually received the money yet. Can you get them back into a state where we can reimburse them?

report.title: Can't send the team their money again
report.description: I backed out the entry for last week's staff costs after spotting the wrong funding account. That entry has vanished from the money-out history, but the individual items still show as settled. Now the screen for putting together another staff payout acts as if we don't owe anyone anything. It offers none of those items, even though we haven't sent the funds. Looks like only half of backing it out took effect.

report.title: Expenses stuck as already paid
report.description: The reimbursement is no longer there, but its expenses still show Paid and can't be picked for another payout.

report.title: Release 6.14 broke reimbursement undo
report.description:
I'm pretty sure this came with Dovetailoop 6.14. We noticed the new release banner this morning, and now we're stuck trying to correct an expense payout. This is our first reimbursement run since that banner appeared, so the timing feels pretty suspicious.

Our studio had seven approved claims ready to pay: travel, printing supplies, and a couple of small purchases for a client workshop. I recorded them together as one reimbursement, then realised I'd chosen our reserve account rather than our day-to-day account. No bank transfer had been made. This was just the record in the app, and I wanted to correct it before handing the payment details to our bookkeeper.

I opened that reimbursement and used Undo. It disappeared from the reimbursement history, and I can no longer find its transaction in the account view. So far, so good. But each of the seven expense claims still has the Paid label. Their amounts and receipts are all still there; it's specifically their payment state that seems wrong.

When I start another reimbursement, none of those seven appears in the selection list. A separate, newly approved expense does appear, so this isn't an empty list or a general loading issue. I've refreshed, signed out and back in, and asked another admin to check. We both see the same thing.

Please don't suggest submitting all seven expenses again. We'd end up with duplicate paperwork and a very confused bookkeeper. We need the existing claims available for the corrected reimbursement. Is there a fix for whatever changed in 6.14, or can support repair these records?

report.title: Reimbursement undo works; expense notes lose text
report.description: Undoing a reimbursement works fine for us now: the transaction disappears, the claims do not stay marked Paid, and we can include them in a replacement reimbursement batch. That's not what this ticket is about. Our complaint is the expense notes box. It lets us type a long explanation, but after saving and reopening the expense, everything beyond about 200 characters is missing. There's no character counter or warning. We need either the full note saved or a visible limit before we submit it.

report.title: Staff without margin access can still open the dashboard from an old shortcut
report.description:
Pasting this from our internal chat because it looks like a permissions issue rather than a missing menu item.

At Tessel Finch Studio, our designers can log time and submit expenses, but only the two owners should be able to see project margins. We checked the affected person's role and the permission to view financial margins is definitely switched off.

After the Quivell 3.9 update, the project-margin dashboard disappeared from their navigation, which is what we expected. However, one designer had saved a dashboard shortcut before we tightened their access. They clicked that shortcut yesterday and the whole page loaded: revenue, costs, margin percentages, and the individual project figures. These are current numbers, not just an old screenshot or an empty page shell.

We asked them to sign out and back in, then try again. Same result. We also tested with a second ordinary staff account that has never had margin access. Giving that account the same destination lets it see the figures too, even though there is no menu option for getting there normally.

Nothing seems wrong with time entry or expense submission. The concern is specifically that hiding the dashboard link hasn't stopped people from reading the underlying margin information. We need the destination itself to refuse access when the person's role doesn't allow it.

Could someone treat this as a confidentiality issue? We have asked staff not to use the shortcut, but that's not an access control, and we can't tell whether anyone else has kept it.

report.title: An old browser favorite reveals earnings figures to a designer
report.description: Our designer's account is meant for logging hours and submitting receipts, not reviewing how much the agency earns on each job. The profitability screen is no longer in their sidebar, but an old browser favorite still takes them straight to the full breakdown of fees minus costs. We changed a cost entry as a test and their figures refreshed too, so this isn't leftover content. Can you make that screen refuse entry for this role rather than just removing its menu link?

report.title: Private margin figures visible to staff
report.description: A staff account that isn't allowed to view project margins can still see the margin dashboard.

report.title: Quivell 4.2 seems to have broken margin privacy
report.description: I'm blaming the 4.2 release because we first noticed this right after upgrading. Our production coordinator has no permission to view financial margins, and the dashboard isn't listed in their menu. But their saved dashboard shortcut still opens the project-margin page with all the live totals. We rechecked the role settings and tried a fresh login; neither changed it. Please investigate what 4.2 did to access restrictions.

report.title: Margin restriction works, but daily digest ignores our chosen time
report.description: The restricted-member test is fine now: staff without permission cannot see the project-margin dashboard, including through a saved dashboard shortcut. No margin figures are exposed. My actual complaint is that the daily activity digest arrives at 03:00 even though our workspace setting says 09:00. Changing the delivery time and saving it again makes no difference. This is the email summary of yesterday's activity, not a dashboard access issue.

report.title: Bulk expense tagging only keeps the first tag
report.description: We selected eight expenses in Foliofern and used the bulk editor to add both “Client work” and “Travel.” After saving, every expense had “Client work” but no “Travel.” Tried again with the tags selected in the opposite order, and then only “Travel” stuck. There’s no warning; it looks like the update worked until we reopen the expenses. Adding both tags to each expense separately works, but doing that across a month of purchases is going to take ages.

report.title: Group changes lose our extra labels
report.description: Picked a whole page of purchases and assigned “Studio supplies,” “Reclaimable,” and “Spring campaign” together. Once the page refreshed, each row showed just “Studio supplies.” If I put “Spring campaign” at the front of the chooser instead, that’s the one left afterward. Going into each purchase’s own details lets all three stay attached. Can the group action do the same?

report.title: Extra expense labels won't stick
report.description: When we change labels on expenses together, only the first one stays; the others disappear.

report.title: Release 4.18 seems to have broken multi-tag expense updates
report.description:
Pasting this from our studio admin channel because it’s holding up our month-end tidy-up. I think the Foliofern 4.18 release is responsible. We noticed this after the new navigation arrived, although I can’t honestly say when we last tried the same operation before that.

I had 26 expenses selected, mostly materials and travel purchases for our fictional client, Brindle Orchard Studio. In the bulk edit panel I chose “Project Alder,” “Billable,” and “Receipt checked,” then saved. The confirmation appeared normally and the panel closed. Looking down the list afterward, all 26 had “Project Alder,” but neither of the other two tags was there.

At first I assumed I hadn’t clicked the options properly. I repeated it with just three expenses and made sure all three chips were visible before pressing Save. Same result. Then I removed the tags and tried choosing “Receipt checked” before the other two. That time “Receipt checked” was the only tag that remained, so it isn’t a particular tag being rejected.

The odd part is that I can open one expense, add all three tags there, save, and reopen it with everything intact. That’s our workaround, but we have several hundred expenses to sort and I really don’t want the team doing them one at a time.

No error banner or failed-update message appeared during any of these attempts. Could you check whether something changed in 4.18? I’m blaming that release because of the timing, not because I have anything more concrete to point to.

report.title: Bulk tags are fine; receipt previews are sideways
report.description: Just to rule out the question from the earlier support reply: bulk expense tagging does NOT keep only the first selected tag for us. We can apply two or more tags, save, and reopen the expenses with all of them present. The actual issue is that portrait receipt photos appear sideways in the preview pane. The original download is upright. Can we rotate the preview without changing the uploaded file?

report.title: Can't reach Save when adding a client with the keyboard
report.description: Pasted from Tavi at Mothglass Studio: In Draftwharf, I can tab through all the new-client fields, but after Notes the focus jumps back to the client name. Save and Cancel never get a turn. Shift+Tab goes around the fields in reverse, also skipping those two buttons. I work without a mouse, so I'm stuck with a filled-in form I can't submit. Escape closes it, but then I lose what I entered.

unlisted_problem.title: Keyboard focus trapped in new-client dialog
unlisted_problem.summary: Keyboard-only users cannot move focus from the final field to the Save or Cancel controls in the new-client dialog. The dialog's focus loop excludes its footer buttons.

report.title: Tomorrow's invoice reminder went out today
report.description: Support ticket from Rella, billing lead at Pebblekite Design: Our Draftwharf workspace is set to UTC−08:00. Invoice PK-208 is due on 18 March, but the client received the due-date reminder on the afternoon of 17 March, our local time. The invoice itself still shows 18 March. This happened with two other invoices last week too. We checked that these are the reminders meant to go out on the due date, not the advance reminders. Can you stop them arriving early? Clients are asking whether we've shortened their payment terms.

unlisted_problem.title: Due-date reminders arrive one day early
unlisted_problem.summary: Invoice due-date reminder emails are sent one calendar day early for workspaces in sufficiently negative time-zone offsets. The scheduler interprets the due date as midnight UTC rather than workspace-local midnight.

report.title: Deleted receipts, still at the storage limit
report.description: From the Fernspool Creative support thread: We permanently deleted about 240 MB of old receipt attachments in Draftwharf. They're gone from the expense claims, but storage still says 998 MB used out of 1 GB, even after signing out and checking again the next morning. We still can't upload this month's receipts.

unlisted_problem.title: Deleted attachments do not release storage quota
unlisted_problem.summary: Permanently deleting receipt attachments removes the files from expense claims but does not reduce the workspace's reported storage usage. The quota counter is not decremented after file deletion.

report.title: Updating a team member's cost changed our closed project margins
report.description:
Slack paste from Nemi at Lanternfold Agency:

I updated Ollo's hourly cost from 36 to 43 credits this morning because the new rate starts this month. Then I opened the profitability report for our completed Winter Window project and its labor cost had gone up. We haven't added hours, edited time entries, or reopened the project.

I downloaded last month's PDF before making the change, so I compared the numbers. The old report has Ollo's 80 hours costing 2,880 credits. The current report shows the same 80 hours costing 3,440 credits. That's exactly the new rate applied to all those old hours.

Those costs were already reviewed and used in our quarterly summary. I need the higher rate for new work without changing what earlier projects cost us. Is there somewhere to enter a start date for a rate change? I only found the one hourly-cost field on the member profile. For now I've put the old value back, but that means our current project estimates are wrong instead.

unlisted_problem.title: Cost-rate edits rewrite historical project costs
unlisted_problem.summary: Changing a member's hourly cost rate recalculates previously recorded project costs using the new rate. The product lacks effective-dated cost rates, so historical profitability changes unexpectedly.

report.title: Full invoice number finds nothing
report.description: Ticket from Brindle Arc Studio: Searching Draftwharf for BA-1047 returns no invoices. Searching just 1047 finds the exact invoice, and its reference is visibly BA-1047. Copied and pasted the whole reference to rule out a typo.

unlisted_problem.title: Invoice search misses hyphenated references
unlisted_problem.summary: Searching for a complete invoice reference containing a hyphen returns no results even when that invoice exists. The search index splits references into tokens, but exact-reference queries are not normalized the same way.

report.title: Translated invoice has untranslated payment buttons
report.description: Vessa from Driftloom Design says: Our workspace language in Draftwharf is English, and we've selected Spanish for client Saffron Pier Atelier. The invoice descriptions and headings are correctly in Spanish. However, when the client opens the hosted payment page, the buttons still say 'Pay now' and 'Download invoice' in English. I tested a newly issued invoice as well as the original link. Changing the client's language doesn't seem to affect those controls, so the page looks only partly translated.

unlisted_problem.title: Payment page ignores the selected client language
unlisted_problem.summary: The hosted invoice payment page displays its action buttons in the workspace language instead of the language selected for the client. Invoice content is translated correctly, leaving the payment page with mixed-language text.

report.title: Holiday week still shows everyone with 40 hours
report.description:
Slack from the planning channel at Paperfen Studio:
We added Founders' Rest on Wednesday to the workspace holiday calendar in Draftwharf. It shows up on the weekly capacity grid, so the date seems to be saved correctly. But each full-time person still has 40 available hours that week instead of 32. After assigning 32 hours, the planner says they have another 8 free. Nobody is working that Wednesday. Are we missing another setting, or do we have to manually reduce everyone's availability every time there's a holiday?

unlisted_problem.title: Capacity planning counts workspace holidays as available time
unlisted_problem.summary: The weekly capacity view includes full working hours on dates configured as workspace holidays. Holiday calendars are displayed visually but are not used in available-hours calculations.

report.title: Need separate expense exemption reasons for two jurisdictions
report.description:
Support request from Kelvi at Thistlewake Creative: We claim expenses across the fictional jurisdictions of Orinth Reach and Velassa Vale. The same untaxed expense can need different exemption reasons: 'registered studio relief' for Orinth Reach and 'out-of-district creative service' for Velassa Vale.

In Draftwharf's expense tax settings, we can mark something exempt, but we can't find a way to keep a separate reason for each jurisdiction. A single shared label won't work for our records. We've started keeping a spreadsheet alongside the claims, which means our accountant has to match every exported expense back to that sheet. Is there a supported way to store both distinctions on the expense rather than burying them in a general note?

unlisted_problem.title: Expense tax settings lack jurisdiction-specific exemptions
unlisted_problem.summary: Expense tax configuration cannot represent different exemption reasons for separate tax jurisdictions. Agencies operating across multiple fictional jurisdictions must store those distinctions outside the product.

report.title: Each department needs its own invoice counter
report.description: From Dovra, operations at Coppermoss Agency: We have separate billing desks for Brand and Motion. Each needs its own sequence: BR-001, BR-002 and MO-001, MO-002. In Draftwharf I can change the invoice prefix, but the next number still comes from the same workspace counter. After BR-018, the next Motion invoice becomes MO-019 rather than MO-006. We need both departments in one workspace for time tracking and bank reconciliation. Can we configure independent counters without splitting the agency into two workspaces?

unlisted_problem.title: Invoice numbering cannot restart separately by department
unlisted_problem.summary: The product supports one invoice-number sequence per workspace but not independent sequences for departments. Agencies with separate departmental billing processes cannot configure their required numbering structure.

report.title: Changing my avatar switched email alerts back on
report.description: Slack paste from Selli at Cloudreed Studio: I uploaded a new profile photo in Draftwharf yesterday, and today I'm getting every email alert again. I'd turned off time-entry nudges and expense-status emails. Both toggles were back on when I checked. I disabled them, uploaded a different photo to test, and they immediately returned to the default settings. The photo saves fine; it's the notification choices that don't stay put.

unlisted_problem.title: Notification preferences reset after profile photo changes
unlisted_problem.summary: Uploading a new profile photo resets that member's email-notification preferences to the defaults. The profile update replaces the preference object instead of preserving its existing values.
